extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties to inter partes review (IPR) proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, PTAB counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: A Patent Trial and Appeal Board Final Written Decision resolving patentability challenges in an inter partes review, applying statutory standards (35 U.S.C. §§ 102, 103, 318) and Board/regulatory claim-construction and evidentiary rules to determine whether claims are unpatentable. Contains legal standards, evidentiary burdens, claim construction guidance, and reasoning on anticipation/obviousness for the challenged claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in IPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must prove unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence; the Board issues a Final Written Decision under 35 U.S.C. § 318(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Written Decision addresses issues and arguments raised during trial; parties seeking judicial review must comply with notice/service requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 90.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation (35 U.S.C. § 102) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: To be anticipated, each and every element of the claim must be found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claim elements are inherently taught, the result must be a necessary consequence of what was deliberately intended, but the prior art need not demonstrate that the authors appreciated the results (citing Atofina, Mehl/Biophile, Schering).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness (35 U.S.C. § 103) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness is determined by looking to the scope and content of the prior art, differences between the prior art and the claims at issue, and the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art (Graham factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may take account of inferences and creative steps a person of ordinary skill would employ (KSR). A claimed invention is unpatentable if differences render it obvious to a POSITA as of the effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the person of ordinary skill in the art based on the nature of the claimed invention and the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For method claims directed to treating patients, relevant POSITA may include clinicians (medical doctors) with experience treating cancer or with access to clinical-study expertise, as well as persons with research experience in immunology/genetics/clinical trials; determine scope from record and claim focus. Expert witnesses' qualifications must be supported; Board will accept testimony absent specific contrary argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are construed in accordance with the ordinary and customary meaning of the claim as understood by one of ordinary skill in the art and the prosecution history pertaining to the patent (37 C.F.R. § 42.100(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board construes disputed terms in light of intrinsic evidence; parties' proposed constructions, prosecution arguments, and district-court positions are considered but do not bind the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'In response to' claim-term interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'in response to' requires a causal relationship wherein the patient must be tested and, if determined to be MSI-H or dMMR, then the patient is treated with pembrolizumab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This causal relationship differs from 'after'; however, the Board declined to import negative limitations excluding treatment of other patients not recited in the claim. The claim's scope is limited to what is recited; do not read unclaimed negative limitations into claim terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-ended transitional phrase 'comprising'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Comprising' in a method claim indicates the claim is open-ended and allows for additional steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because 'comprising' is open-ended, additional steps taken in conjunction with the recited method steps are not excluded from claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherency principle and effect on efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a prior-art reference discloses steps that necessarily produce a claimed result, the result can be inherent even if the prior authors did not appreciate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If efficacy is a necessary consequence of the prior-art steps (e.g., dosage and treatment regimen disclosed), efficacy can be inherent and support anticipation; Mehl/Biophile cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and procedural context inference from prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether prior-art disclosures (e.g., clinical study records) teach the timing of steps (such as testing before enrollment/treatment) by examining study design, arms, eligibility, enrollment and practical realities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A POSITA can infer procedural timing (e.g., that MSI testing occurred before enrollment) from the study's design, expected enrollment numbers, and practical requirements to achieve the reported outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation to combine and reasonable expectation of success (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish obviousness over multiple references, show that a POSITA would have been motivated to combine the teachings of the prior art and would have had a reasonable expectation of success in doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation can derive from the prior-art teachings (e.g., Pernot motivating use of PD-1 inhibitors in MSI cancers) and routine nature of combining standard testing methods; expectation of success can be satisfied even when results become inherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dependent-claim limitations in obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: When independent claims are shown to be anticipated, dependent claims may still be analyzed for obviousness over additional references for discrete limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner must specifically rebut obviousness for dependent-claim limitations; failure to address discrete limitations may permit Board to find them obvious if prior art supplies them with motivation and expectation of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary considerations (objective indicia) and nexus requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of industry praise, skepticism, long-felt need, unexpected results, and commercial success may be considered, but Patent Owner bears the burden to show a nexus between that evidence and the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the independent claims are anticipated, secondary considerations cannot overcome anticipation. If the asserted evidence relates exclusively to a feature known in the prior art (coextensive with prior art), it is not persuasive of non-obviousness (citing Yita, Cohesive, Ethicon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on incorporation by reference for arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments must not be incorporated by reference from one document into another; combined documents and incorporation by reference of arguments are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a)(3); parties must present arguments directly in each filing and may not rely on incorporation-by-reference to supply omitted content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board's treatment of expert testimony (disregard requires specific argument)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will not disregard an expert's testimony in general absent specific argument challenging particular testimony or qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party asserting an expert is unqualified must present specific arguments; mere conclusory objections without pinpointed flaws are insufficient to negate the testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: When anticipation obviates need for separate obviousness analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims are found anticipated by a prior art reference, they may also be obvious, and the Board need not separately analyze obviousness for claims already anticipated in a ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where anticipation is found for claims, Board may limit additional obviousness review to claims not included in anticipation grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural handling of sealed/sealable material and redactions
rubrics_metrics.description: If portions of the decision include sealed material, parties may meet and confer and may submit proposed redacted public versions with motions to seal within seven days of entry of the Final Written Decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any opposition to a sealing motion must be filed within ten days after the motion is filed; absent timely motions or notice that redactions are unnecessary, the Final Written Decision will be made public unredacted.
